_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-14 · Sky155 — Sierra now names the colleges AND links them, and her built-in rules are finally editable.
_status: Five fixes shipped today, all from things you hit while testing. Sierra now answers a "where can I get credit for this?" question with the colleges that have ALREADY set it up, each with a link to its CPL page — the links were the missing half, and the reason they were missing is that nobody had ever handed them to her, even though we have had them for 123 of 123 colleges all along. That is the fourth time we have found good data sitting unread. The bigger change is underneath: the ten built-in rules that tell Sierra how to behave used to live only in code, which is why an instruction you wrote at 1:33pm could be quietly overruled by a rule you could not see or edit. Those rules are now in a table. Nothing about her answers changed on day one — we proved that letter-for-letter — but from here a rule can be reworded without a code release, and we can now show which rules were in play for any given answer. The safety-critical ones (never invent a college, never expose a small student count) are deliberately locked so no edit can remove them. Also: the Send note box now tells you when it actually sent, the side menu has lost its emoji, and testing an instruction will keep working even if you hide the CPL Assistant tab.

items.text: Two questions before the Admin tab gets built, and both change its shape. FIRST: what unlocks Admin itself? It would control which tabs everyone else can see, so my recommendation is a magic-link sign-in only, NOT a shared phrase — someone holding a phrase who can also change what other phrase-holders see is a bigger version of a problem we already have open. SECOND: should Admin absorb the Team Phrases tab? That tab deliberately does not open to a phrase holder, because someone who can rotate the phrase makes rotating it pointless. If Admin is sign-in-only anyway they may be the same door — worth merging on purpose rather than by accident.

Worth knowing before you use the Admin tab to hide things: hiding a menu item does NOT protect the data behind it. It only stops the item being shown. The real lock is on the database, and only two tabs actually lock their data that way — the rest just stop drawing. I will make that distinction visible in the tab itself rather than burying it in a tooltip, because it is the kind of thing that is easy to assume and expensive to be wrong about.

Something to look at when you next test welding. Your AWS D1.1 question got a good answer, but we hold NINE different D1.1 credentials and the answer covered one of them. Riverside has set up three and Lemoore one, and neither college appeared anywhere in the reply — not even in the "teaches welding" list. I have not yet worked out whether she never found them or found them and only showed the strongest, and that difference decides the fix, so I would rather measure it than guess. Recorded so it does not get lost.

The rules table is live and Sierra reads it on every question, but there is no screen to edit it yet — today it takes a database command. The editing screen belongs in the Admin tab, and it should ship together with the "which rules were in play for this answer" view, because seeing that a rule was fighting your instruction is worth more than being able to edit it.

Next after Admin: put what we KNOW (the memory table) and what Sierra DOES (the rules table) on one screen, linked, then have a nightly check report anything decided in memory that no rule actually implements. That gap is what caused three separate problems already, including today's missing links.

The emoji are gone from the side menu — all ten of them. I deliberately left two other kinds alone and want to check that is what you meant: the lock symbol in the header stays, because it changes to show whether you are signed in (that is information, not decoration), and a couple of tabs still show an emoji in their own on-page heading rather than in the menu. Say the word and those go too.
